description: The console window's local grants, and only it. The login webview is absent from every capability, so no command resolves for it, and that absence is the whole fence. It is not that a marketplace page has no bridge: Tauri injects the IPC internals into every webview it creates regardless of URL (tauri 2.11.5, src/manager/webview.rs:166-200), and app.withGlobalTauri adds window.__TAURI__ on top of them. What a page at a marketplace origin lacks is permission, because its window label is not main and nothing here grants it anything. This capability carries no remote block, so nothing in it reaches remote content: the plugin and core permissions here are the ones the bundled fallback page needs, and the application's own console commands are granted separately in console.json, to one named origin and to local content as well — local because the development override serves the console from the vite origin, where the window is local content and a remote-only grant would refuse every command in development. The one exception is allow-retry-console, which is here because the page that calls it is the bundled fallback shown when the control plane cannot be reached: that page runs at the Tauri origin, where the console never does, and it can reach nothing on its own. Splitting them is what stops a widening of the console grant silently widening the updater's. The updater's own grant has since moved out of this file entirely, to updater.json, because tauri-plugin-updater is no longer a dependency of the Android build and a capability naming a permission whose plugin is absent fails the build rather than being ignored: `Permission updater:default not found`. That file carries the platform list this one deliberately does not. One thing about that fence reads differently on Android and is recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered: there is one Activity, so a marketplace login cannot have a window of its own and instead replaces the console inside window main — the very label every capability here names. What refuses a marketplace page there is therefore not the absent label but the per-invoke remote-origin check (tauri 2.11.5, src/webview/mod.rs), tested against the one origin console.json grants. That check is only as good as the origin list, which is what control_plane::the_capability_grants_the_origin_this_build_uses asserts is exactly one entry and equal to DEFAULT_BASE_URL.
